description: Published on Main is Vancouver's leading modern Canadian fine-dining address, combining precise technique with the forests, waters and foraged flavours of British Columbia. Its North America's 50 Best ranking and Michelin star make it the city's clearest international destination restaurant.
highlights: Michelin-starred tasting-menu restaurant with foraged B.C. ingredients, creative cocktails and current North America 50 Best status.
sources: Michelin Guide; North America's 50 Best Restaurants; Canada's 100 Best; Published on Main

description: AnnaLena brings special-occasion Canadian cooking to Kitsilano with polished tasting menus, warm service and a room that balances refinement with playful personality. Its Michelin star and 2026 North America's 50 Best debut keep it at the top of Vancouver's affluent dining set.
highlights: Kitsilano fine dining with contemporary Canadian menus, warm hospitality and North America 50 Best recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide; North America's 50 Best Restaurants; Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine

description: Kissa Tanto remains one of Vancouver's most seductive rooms, pairing Japanese-Italian cooking with the atmosphere of a 1960s Tokyo jazz cafe. The Michelin-starred Chinatown restaurant is as much a design and mood statement as it is a technically ambitious dinner reservation.
highlights: Moody Chinatown loft, Japanese-Italian fusion, deep wine list and one of the city's most distinctive atmospheres.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Conde Nast Traveler; Kissa Tanto

description: Sumibiyaki Arashi is Vancouver's intimate benchmark for omakase-style yakitori and charcoal grilling. With only a handful of seats and a Michelin star, it gives affluent diners a focused, elemental counter experience built around smoke, patience and precision.
highlights: Fourteen-seat Michelin-starred yakitori counter with charcoal technique, seasonal courses and an immersive Mount Pleasant format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Conde Nast Traveler; Sumibiyaki Arashi

description: St. Lawrence channels Quebecois and classic French cooking through a compact, highly personal Vancouver dining room. The restaurant's Michelin star, rigorous set menus and deep sense of place make it one of the city's most characterful destination bookings.
highlights: Michelin-starred Quebecois-French tasting menus, intimate room and one of Vancouver's strongest service identities.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; St. Lawrence

description: Okeya Kyujiro turns omakase into theatre, presenting sushi, seasonal dishes and Japanese hospitality in a carefully choreographed counter format. Its Michelin star and premium pricing make it one of downtown Vancouver's most formal Japanese reservations.
highlights: Michelin-starred theatrical omakase with a 25-course dinner format and downtown counter setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Okeya Kyujiro

description: Masayoshi is a jewel-box sushi counter where chef Masayoshi Baba applies Japanese discipline to Pacific Northwest seafood. The Michelin-starred Fraserhood room feels quiet, exacting and personal, with an omakase format built for serious sushi diners.
highlights: Michelin-starred sushi counter, hyper-seasonal omakase and a refined Japanese room in Fraserhood.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; 50 Best Discovery; Masayoshi

description: Sushi Masuda is an intensely small omakase counter on West Hastings, led by a Vancouver-born chef trained in Tokyo. Its Michelin star, five-seat scale and reservation-only rhythm make it one of the city's most serious sushi experiences.
highlights: Five-seat Michelin-starred omakase counter with Tokyo training, seasonal fish and a highly personal pace.
sources: Michelin Guide; Sushi Masuda; Daily Hive; OpenTable

description: Sushi Hyun is a polished West End omakase restaurant that hides a refined sushi experience behind an understated facade. The Michelin-starred counter offers seasonal fish, elegant pacing and the kind of focused intimacy that Vancouver's top Japanese dining audience seeks.
highlights: Michelin-starred West End omakase with more than 15 courses, seasonal fish and an intimate counter format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tock; OpenTable; Washoku Guide

description: Burdock & Co is Andrea Carlson's Mount Pleasant restaurant devoted to farm-to-table British Columbia cooking and a strong natural-wine sensibility. It remains one of Vancouver's most influential Michelin-starred rooms for diners who care about sustainability, locality and flavour over formality.
highlights: Michelin-starred Pacific Northwest cooking, local farms, natural wines and a low-key Mount Pleasant room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Destination Vancouver; Vancouver Magazine

description: iDen & QuanJuDe brings the Beijing roast-duck house tradition to Vancouver in a polished, theatrical fine-dining format. Its Michelin star, tableside duck service and historic Quanjude lineage give the city a rare Chinese luxury-dining landmark.
highlights: Michelin-starred Beijing duck specialist with imperial culinary heritage, polished service and tableside carving.
sources: Michelin Guide; iDen & QuanJuDe; Vancouver Magazine

description: Barbara is an intimate tasting-menu counter where chef Patrick Hennessy gives local ingredients a precise, personal treatment. The Michelin-starred room is small, adult and quietly theatrical, suited to diners who like to watch the kitchen work at close range.
highlights: Small Michelin-starred counter restaurant with a tasting menu, local ingredients and a chef-at-work atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Barbara

description: Le Crocodile is one of Vancouver's great French dining institutions, newly sharpened under Rob Feenie while retaining its polished downtown DNA. It is the natural choice for Dover sole, classic sauces, serious wine and a grown-up room that still feels celebratory.
highlights: Reimagined French institution on Burrard Street with Rob Feenie, classic luxury dishes and a deep wine cellar.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; OpenTable; En Primeur Club

description: Baan Lao is a Steveston destination that brings Royal Thai cooking into a formal tasting-menu setting on the waterfront. It sits outside Vancouver proper, but its national ranking, design, ceremony and culinary specificity make it a credible luxury-dining excursion from the city.
highlights: Royal Thai tasting-menu destination in Steveston with waterfront atmosphere and strong national recognition.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; World Culinary Awards; OpenTable; Baan Lao

description: June on Cambie gives Vancouver a stylish new brasserie-and-bar room with serious design, a strong drinks program and a social dinner energy. It is less formal than the Michelin tier, but its Canada 100 Best recognition and polished room make it relevant for affluent, design-conscious diners.
highlights: Design-led Cambie brasserie with cocktail pedigree, contemporary comfort cooking and a strong evening scene.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; North America's 50 Best Bars; June on Cambie

description: Boulevard is a polished downtown seafood room inside the Sutton Place Hotel, balancing oyster-bar energy with serious culinary credentials. Chef Alex Chen's kitchen, a strong pastry program and Michelin recommendation keep it among Vancouver's most reliable luxury-hotel dining choices.
highlights: Michelin-recommended seafood restaurant with oyster bar, polished hotel setting and award-winning culinary team.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Sutton Place Hotel; Vancouver Magazine

description: Botanist sits above the Fairmont Pacific Rim lobby as a lush, polished expression of modern Pacific Northwest dining. The garden-like room, cocktail lab and refined sourcing make it a natural fit for luxury hotel guests and Vancouver locals planning a celebratory night.
highlights: Fairmont Pacific Rim dining room with botanical design, modern Canadian cooking, cocktail lab and strong wine program.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Fairmont Pacific Rim; Vancouver Magazine

description: Hawksworth remains a downtown Vancouver landmark for ingredient-led contemporary Canadian cooking in the Rosewood Hotel Georgia. The Studio Munge-designed rooms, central luxury-hotel address and refined service keep it firmly in the city's affluent dining conversation.
highlights: Rosewood Hotel Georgia dining landmark with contemporary Canadian cuisine, elegant rooms and a serious wine-and-cocktail program.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Rosewood Hotel Georgia; The Australian

description: Bacchus is the old-world dining room of the Wedgewood Hotel, all European polish, live-piano romance and classic service. Its Canada 100 Best placement confirms that the room's enduring luxury still speaks to contemporary Vancouver diners.
highlights: Relais and Chateaux hotel dining room with Venetian touches, classic cuisine, live music and romantic downtown atmosphere.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; Relais & Chateaux; Dine Out Vancouver; Wedgewood Hotel

description: Elisa is Yaletown's polished wood-fired steak and seafood restaurant, built for affluent diners who want energy, meat, wine and service rather than a tasting-menu format. Its Michelin recommendation, international steakhouse ranking and sommelier recognition make it more than a conventional grill.
highlights: Wood-fired steak and seafood in Yaletown with deep wine service, Michelin recommendation and strong international steakhouse recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide; 101 Best Steak Restaurants; Vancouver Magazine; Elisa

description: Chez Celine is J-C Poirier's more relaxed French-Quebecois sibling to St. Lawrence, trading tasting-menu precision for generous brasserie pleasure. The Fraser Street room has quickly become a serious affluent-casual booking thanks to national recognition and a confident, adult sense of hospitality.
highlights: Award-winning French-Quebecois bistro from the St. Lawrence team with generous cooking and a polished neighborhood feel.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; Conde Nast Traveler; My VanCity

description: Elem is a design-forward Mount Pleasant restaurant from chef Vish Mayekar, bringing global technique, a striking room and inventive cocktails into a modern Vancouver format. Its rapid Michelin recommendation and Canada 100 Best placement make it one of the city's strongest newer affluent-dining entries.
highlights: Michelin-recommended Mount Pleasant restaurant with global cooking, no-waste cocktails and a thoughtfully designed room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; OpenTable

description: Kavita gives Vancouver a refined modern Indian tasting-menu restaurant grounded in regional traditions and British Columbia ingredients. Chef Tushar Tondvalkar's background in serious kitchens and the restaurant's Canada 100 Best recognition make it a distinctive addition to the city's high-end core.
highlights: Modern Indian tasting-menu restaurant with regional Indian references, local B.C. produce and a polished Mount Pleasant room.
sources: Canada's 100 Best; Vancouver Magazine; OpenTable; Restaurant Kavita

description: Blue Water Cafe is Vancouver's definitive Yaletown seafood restaurant, pairing a raw bar and sushi counter with the polish of a classic special-occasion room. It remains a concierge-safe answer for pristine seafood, good wine and a grown-up downtown crowd.
highlights: Yaletown seafood institution with raw bar, sushi, serious wine and polished Toptable service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater; Conde Nast Traveler; Blue Water Cafe

description: L'Abattoir turns a historic Gastown building into one of Vancouver's most enduring French-influenced West Coast dining rooms. It is polished enough for business dinners and special occasions, with a serious wine program, cocktails and a menu that has shaped the city's modern restaurant identity.
highlights: Historic Gastown room with elevated West Coast-French cooking, award-winning wine and cocktail programs.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater; Conde Nast Traveler; L'Abattoir

description: Tojo's is a foundational Vancouver Japanese institution, still trading on chef Hidekazu Tojo's Pacific Northwest omakase legacy and world-famous role in modern sushi culture. It is not the newest sushi room in town, but its history, premium pricing and ongoing dinner service keep it relevant for culinary travelers.
highlights: World-renowned Japanese fine-dining institution with seasonal omakase, Pacific Northwest ingredients and California Roll lore.
sources: Tojo's; OpenTable; City of Vancouver business licence; Washoku Guide

description: Miku is the waterfront flagship that introduced Aburi-style sushi to Vancouver and helped define the city's modern Japanese-Canadian dining vocabulary. The room's harbour views, full sushi bar and polished service make it a strong high-end alternative for a less formal evening.
highlights: Waterfront Aburi sushi flagship with harbour views, private dining and Michelin Guide recommendation.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Miku Vancouver; Destination Vancouver

description: CinCin is a long-running Robson Street Italian room with wood-fired cooking, a celebrated grill program and an elegant upstairs setting. It delivers a polished, social kind of luxury that works for business dinners, couples and visitors who want Vancouver's classic downtown restaurant rhythm.
highlights: Wood-fired Italian dining on Robson Street with an elegant room, established reputation and lively downtown energy.
sources: Vancouver Magazine; CinCin; Conde Nast Traveler; OpenTable

description: Maenam is Angus An's Kitsilano Thai flagship, pairing bold regional Thai flavours with pristine West Coast ingredients and one of Vancouver's more thoughtful beverage approaches. It is relaxed in tone, but its Michelin recommendation, longevity and culinary precision make it a genuine instead-of-Michelin option.
highlights: Michelin-recommended modern Thai restaurant with seasonal B.C. ingredients, strong Riesling pairings and long-running local respect.
sources: Michelin Guide; Maenam; Vancouver Magazine; OpenTable

description: Ancora's False Creek location combines Nikkei flavours, sustainable seafood and one of Vancouver's most useful waterfront settings for an affluent dinner. The patio, caviar-and-raw-bar options and Peruvian-Japanese menu give it an easy luxury-hospitality appeal.
highlights: False Creek waterfront restaurant with Peruvian-Japanese seafood, sushi, cocktails and patio views.
sources: Destination Vancouver; Dine Out Vancouver; OpenTable; Ancora

description: Savio Volpe is one of Vancouver's most beloved modern osterias, built around wood fire, rustic Italian cooking and a room that always feels alive. It is informal compared with the fine-dining tier, but sophisticated diners value it for warmth, consistency and genuine local affection.
highlights: Lively Kingsway osteria with wood-fired Italian cooking, chef's-choice feasts and strong neighborhood loyalty.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Savio Volpe; Vancouver Magazine

description: Vij's is a defining Vancouver restaurant, making refined Indian cooking feel generous, social and unmistakably local. The Cambie Village room remains a relaxed but serious dinner choice for travelers who want cultural significance without a formal tasting-menu structure.
highlights: Iconic Vancouver Indian restaurant with Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition, cocktails and a celebratory local following.
sources: Michelin Guide; Vij's; Eater; Vancouver Magazine

description: Phnom Penh is the Chinatown institution Vancouver locals still line up for, especially for chicken wings, butter beef and Cambodian-Vietnamese comfort dishes. It is not polished luxury, but it is a culturally essential relaxed dinner that a well-traveled diner should understand.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand Chinatown institution known for butter beef, chicken wings and a lively Cambodian-Vietnamese menu.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater; Bon Appetit; Restaurantji

description: Sun Sui Wah is a classic Vancouver Cantonese seafood room, known for dim sum, live seafood and banquet-style dinners. Its Main Street dining room is relaxed rather than fashionable, but the restaurant's longevity and Cantonese identity make it a meaningful local favorite.
highlights: Long-running Cantonese seafood and dim sum institution with roasted squab, lobster and banquet-style dinners.
sources: Sun Sui Wah; Eater; Restaurantji; Vancouver Magazine

description: Salmon n' Bannock gives Vancouver a rare Indigenous-owned dining room focused on ingredients and food traditions from Turtle Island. The room is modest, but its cultural role, warm hospitality and wild salmon, game and bannock dishes make it an important relaxed dinner for thoughtful visitors.
highlights: Indigenous-owned Vancouver bistro with wild salmon, game meats, bannock and strong cultural storytelling.
sources: Indigenous Tourism BC; Destination Indigenous; Conde Nast Traveler; Salmon n' Bannock
